title: Localization preserves a presented algebra colimit
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and s∈R. A homomorphism of R-algebras A→B induces the map A[1/s]→B[1/s] specified on the image of A. These maps preserve identities, composition and the structural map R[1/s]. Suppose a nonempty family of R-algebras D_i, transition maps along a relation, and inclusions D_i→F exhibit F as their colimit against all ring targets. Then the induced localized maps exhibit F[1/s] as the colimit of D_i[1/s], with the same uniqueness property against ring targets.

proof.text: Construct the localized map with IsLocalization.Away.lift. The denominator maps to a unit because the original map fixes coefficients. Its formula on A is the localization lift equation. Check identity, composition and structural-map compatibility on A or R by localization extensionality.

Restrict a compatible family on the localized levels to the original levels. The original universal property gives g:F→Q. At any chosen level the image of s is a unit; compatibility identifies it with g(s), so g extends to F[1/s]→Q. Check this extension on each localized level by localization extensionality. If another extension agrees on all localized levels, its restriction to F equals g by the original colimit property, and localization extensionality makes the extensions equal.

proof_origin.place: 00CO localization and 04AX colimit universal properties. Explicit universal-property assembly of the displayed constructions.
